statement.text: A '''quasi-kernel''' of a digraph <math>D</math> is an independent vertex set <math>K</math>   sucht that every vertex  is reachable from <math>K</math>  in <math>D</math> by a path of length at most two. A '''quasi-sink''' of <math>D</math> is a quasi-kernel of the digraph that we obtain by changing the direction of the edges in <math>D</math>. Is it true that for any infinite digraph <math>D=(V,A)</math> there is a partition <math>\{V_1, V_2\}</math> of <math>V</math> such that <math>D[V_1]</math> admits a quasi-kernel and <math>D[V_2]</math> admits a quasi-sink?
